equity_bridge.item: Restructuring cash above the $300m/yr normalised special-items run-rate, 2026-2030 (after tax, PV)
equity_bridge.note: NEW in this update. Special items ran $1,046m pre-tax in FY2025 and $747m in 9M 2026 (Strategic Optimization Program $535m, litigation $126m, integration $92m; Q3 10-Q Note 15), against the $300m/yr the margin anchor deducts. At the 30 Sept 2026 Investor Day the program was extended as 'Accelerate to One' with cost savings 'through 2030', so the excess is no longer a two-year item. Judged excess pre-tax: ~$600m 2026, $500m 2027, $400m 2028, $300m 2029, $200m 2030 = $2.0bn; x (1-21%) discounted at 7.5% ~= $1.2bn. The savings side is credited separately, and only partly, in the base margin path. Company has not disclosed the program's total cost -- replace with the disclosed figure when the FY2026 10-K gives one.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Consolidated pre-tax adjusted income from operations FY2023-FY2025 ($9,318m -> $9,533m -> $9,870m), the company's own post-NCI operating profit series. 9M 2026 is running +7% ($7,803m vs $7,321m) but the FY2026 outlook implies ~+3% for the full year.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-2.1% 3y, -3.6% 5y) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (15.1% / 11.4%): book value shrinks because Cigna buys back ~all earnings, and revenue is inflated by pass-through drug cost (GLP-1/specialty) and the 2024 Centene PBM contract. Neither is a usable growth anchor; operating profit growth (~3%/yr) is.
historical_growth.notes: Annual CAGRs are unchanged from the prior build (no new fiscal year). Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC; no interest income strip as Cigna is net debt): FY2023 $9,954m (OCF 11,813 - capex 1,573 - SBC 286), FY2025 $8,098m (9,601 - 1,212 - 291). Capex is not in the XBRL-built CSV for FY2020-FY2022, so 3y/5y FCF CAGRs are not computed. OCF is lumpy (receivable factoring, rebate timing; 9M 2026 OCF $3,281m), which is why the build is component-based and not anchored on any single year's FCF. GAAP EPS is distorted by the FY2024 VillageMD write-down and FY2023 tax items.

scenario_narratives.base: Evernorth converts to rebate-free/cost-plus pricing (fully insured 2027, all clients 2028) and absorbs the 2028 federal delinking and the FTC consent decree at the cost of roughly 6% of consolidated margin beyond what 2026 has already taken -- Pharmacy Benefit Services income is down a quarter in 2026 on proactive renewals and recontracting, and that has been carried by Specialty and Care Services (+19%) and Cigna Healthcare (+16%). It keeps its Big-Three scale and grows specialty (Accredo, GLP-1 management) volumes. Cigna Healthcare narrows to self-funded employer and international after the IFP exit; MCR holds near 84%. Attributable operating profit is flat-to-down in 2028 and then compounds ~3-4%/yr -- about 9% EPS growth with buybacks, short of management's 10-14% target; part of the Accelerate to One savings reaches the margin and its restructuring cost is charged in the bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: Cost-plus pricing proves a share-winner: employers and health plans consolidate to the most transparent Big-Three PBM, the Shields/specialty investments and biosimilar/GLP-1 programs lift specialty mix, and the September 2026 Investor Day target (10-14% adjusted EPS CAGR through 2030, ~$50bn cumulative operating cash flow) is met near its top. Margin holds through 2028 and edges up to 4.5% on specialty mix and the $3bn productivity program; regulation codifies a model Evernorth has already adopted instead of breaking it.
scenario_narratives.bear: Delinking and spread-pricing bans strip rebate and spread economics faster than service fees replace them -- the 25% drop in Pharmacy Benefit Services income in 2026 is the first instalment, not the whole bill; large clients (the HCSC services agreement, Centene-scale PBM contracts) re-bid on price against CVS TrueCost and Optum Rx cost-plus, and state PBM laws layer on further constraints. Pharmacy customers keep shrinking (117.7m vs 122.5m a year ago). Evernorth margin falls roughly a quarter by 2029, revenue stalls in 2028 as gross-to-net presentation changes, and Cigna Healthcare MCR stays at or above 85% on specialty/GLP-1 trend. Operating profit settles ~25% below the FY2026 level and grows only 2-2.5%; the market's ~9x earnings multiple becomes the right one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Cigna as a fee-and-spread health-services operator, not as an insurer: the cash comes from Evernorth's PBM/specialty scale and ASO fees, and the book value is mostly Express Scripts goodwill that buybacks keep shrinking. The whole valuation turns on how much PBM margin survives the 2027-2028 rebate-free conversion and federal delinking; the base case assumes ~6% further margin loss after a 2026 in which PBM income already fell a quarter, the bear ~27%.
key_risks_to_valuation: PBM delinking (2028) and the FTC consent decree compress Evernorth margins more than modelled; Pharmacy Benefit Services income is already -25% in 9M 2026
Large-client re-bids (HCSC services agreement, health-plan PBM contracts) at cost-plus pricing; pharmacy customers down 4% YoY
Medical cost trend / GLP-1 utilisation keeps Cigna Healthcare MCR above 84% (Q3 2026: 85.0%; FY outlook 84.2% +/- 25bp)
Revenue presentation changes under cost-plus (gross vs net) move the % margins even where dollars do not -- read the scenarios in dollars of operating profit
Investor Day targets (10-14% adjusted EPS CAGR, ~$50bn cumulative OCF through 2030) are only partly credited in the base case; if they are met the base is too low by roughly the base-to-bull gap
Restructuring under Accelerate to One: total cost undisclosed, charged here as a $1.2bn judgment in the equity bridge
Income attributable to noncontrolling interests has more than doubled ($736m 9M 2026 vs $342m); a growing share of consolidated profit is not shareholders'
Continued renewable tax-credit equity investments and specialty investments (Shields, ~$3.5bn) are capital calls not modelled as growth capex

reconciliation.unchanged: Deliberately left alone: the model (owner-FCF component), all growth paths, SBC/D&A/capex/tax paths, working-capital capture, WACC 7.5%, terminal growth and cap multiples, the bull and bear margin paths beyond Y1, and the 30/50/20 weights. What would move them: FY2027 outlook (Feb 2027) for the Y2 growth and margin; disclosed economics of the rebate-free conversion or a large-client re-bid for the 2028 trough; a 10-year Treasury move of >50bp for WACC; a disclosed Accelerate to One cost for the bridge item.

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average Q3 2026 (10-Q 2026-09-30 EPS note: basic 262.790m + 0.998m common stock equivalents = 263.788m). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, buybacks are the funding mechanism (FY2025 $3,621m; 9M 2026 only $531m while cash went to debt reduction; ~$500m / 1.8m shares YTD to 4 Nov 2026).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K, AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $291m (XBRL). Equity-award tax withholding is not separately disclosed (buried in financing 'Other, net'), so SBC is the expense line only; immaterial at ~0.1% of revenue either way.
inputs.ttm_memo: TTM to 2026-09-30: OCF $9,430m (9,601 - 3,452 + 3,281), P&E purchases $1,164m (1,212 - 890 + 842), reported FCF ~$8,266m. fy0 stays FY2025 so last_fcf/reported_fcf are the audited full-year figures.
inputs.wacc_rationale: UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-26 build. USD build. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), beta ~0.7 (managed care/PBM, defensive), ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~7.8%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (interest expense ~$1.4bn on ~$31bn), 4.2% after tax; market D/(D+E) ~26% -> WACC ~6.9%, rounded UP to 7.5% and applied identically to all three scenarios. Regulatory risk (PBM delinking, FTC decree) is charged in the bear driver path and the 30% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases immaterial (~$130m/yr payments, <0.05% of revenue); left inside EBITDA/opex, no lease liability in net debt. One treatment only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: the EBITDA margin is anchored to pre-tax adjusted income from operations, which Cigna reports AFTER income attributable to noncontrolling interests ($736m in 9M 2026 vs $342m in 9M 2025; $475m FY2025). No further NCI deduction in the bridge (book NCI $339m at 2026-09-30). NCI income has more than doubled; because the anchor is post-NCI this is already inside the margin, but it means consolidated EBITDA overstates what shareholders own by a growing amount.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (engine route) -- same model as the 2026-09-26 build; this is an UPDATE. Routing: Cigna is ~90% a health-services/fee business -- Evernorth (PBM, Accredo specialty pharmacy) is ~2/3 of adjusted operating income and Cigna Healthcare is predominantly self-funded/ASO employer business (14.8m ASO of 18.5m medical customers); after the March 2025 sale of Medicare Advantage to HCSC and the 1 Jan 2027 IFP exit the risk-bearing insurance book is a minority. Its cash flow statement is a real operating-company cash flow, so the SKILL.md 'insurer -> BVPS compounding' row does not fit: book value is dominated by ~$73bn of Express Scripts goodwill+intangibles and is managed down by buybacks. Insurance-specific handling: (1) net investment income earned on float investments backing insurance liabilities is left INSIDE the operating margin and those investments are NOT added to the bridge (matching-asset rule, counted once); (2) only balance-sheet cash is netted against financial debt; (3) wc_capture slightly negative for statutory capital that must grow with premiums. MARGIN ANCHOR (unchanged method): FY2025 consolidated pre-tax adjusted income from operations $9,870m (after interest, after NCI, excl. amortization of acquired intangibles and special items) + ~$1,400m interest - ~$300m/yr normalised recurring special items = $10,970m attributable EBIT (3.99% of revenue); + depreciation of P&E/software ~$1,032m + SBC $291m = 4.47% pre-SBC EBITDA margin. Acquired-intangible amortization is excluded from D&A because it is book-only (not tax deductible) -- note it stepped up to $589m in Q3 2026 from $436m, which is why reported D&A jumped to $867m; that does not touch the model. Y1 (FY2026) RE-ANCHORED on the 5 Nov 2026 outlook: adjusted EPS >= $30.60 (raised from $30.45) x 263.8m = $8.07bn; / (1-21%) + interest ~$1.39bn (9M 'interest expense and other' $1,046m) - $0.3bn specials = ~$11.3bn EBIT; + ~$1.04bn depreciation + $0.29bn SBC on ~$290bn revenue (9M total revenue $213.8bn, +5.6% YoY; the company's '~$280bn adjusted revenue' guidance line is running ~3% behind actuals and is not used) -> 4.38% EBITDA margin. 9M 2026 consolidated pre-tax adjusted income from operations $7,803m (+7%); the raised floor implies Q4 adjusted EPS of ~$7.05 vs $8.08 in Q4 2025, i.e. management is guiding a weak Q4 at Evernorth (>= $6.9bn FY against $4,958m at 9M). CASH TAX: cash taxes paid are depressed by 'renewable energy tax credit equity investments' ($312m in 9M 2026, $1,102m FY2025; an investing outflow that buys tax credits); cash tax + those investments ~= book tax, so the model uses the economic 21% rate (9M 2026 adjusted rate 20.3%). CAPEX: 'Property and equipment purchases, net' $842m in 9M 2026 vs $890m (FY2025 $1,212m) -> 0.40-0.46% of revenue; path left at 0.46%. OCF remains lumpy (9M 2026 $3,281m vs $3,452m; Q4 carries the year), which is why the build is component-based. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

bear.rationale: Only Y1 moved (4.30 -> 4.31, the guidance raise). Later years UNCHANGED: the 25% fall in Pharmacy Benefit Services income is the bear mechanism showing up in the numbers, so nothing here is softened; it would be softened if PBS income stabilises through 2027 renewals, and deepened if Specialty and Care Services growth stalls while PBS is still falling.

base.rationale: FY2026 on the raised 5 Nov outlook (4.37 -> 4.38); 2027 IFP exit (unchanged); 2028 cost-plus/delinking conversion now takes ~6% off the margin (4.38% -> 4.10%) instead of ~8% (-> 4.00%), and flattens revenue as rebates stop grossing up; thereafter operating profit grows with specialty/GLP-1 volumes at ~3-4.5%. CHANGED: mature margin 4.00 -> 4.10 and the 2028 transition year 4.10 -> 4.15. Evidence: (a) Pharmacy Benefit Services pre-tax income is already down 25% in 9M 2026 ($1,768m vs $2,352m) on proactive large-client renewals, rebate-free investment and recontracting -- roughly $0.75bn/yr of the repricing the prior path placed in 2028 has been absorbed inside FY2026 guidance, which was nonetheless raised; (b) Specialty and Care Services +19% and Cigna Healthcare +16% are carrying it; (c) the Investor Day target of 10-14% adjusted EPS CAGR through 2030, set after the delinking law was enacted, plus the productivity program. The path still implies only ~2.4%/yr EBIT growth 2026-2030 (~9% EPS with buybacks), BELOW the low end of management's range -- a deliberate haircut. Growth, SBC, D&A, capex, tax, WACC, terminal growth and cap are unchanged.

bull.rationale: Only Y1 moved (4.40 -> 4.41, the guidance raise). Later years UNCHANGED: the path already implied ~6%/yr EBIT growth to 2030, i.e. ~13-14% EPS with buybacks -- the top of the 10-14% range management has now published -- so the Investor Day confirms the bull case as built and gives no reason to lift it.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 30/50/20. Bear stays at 30% (vs the 15% default) because the profit engine still depends on a single regulatory outcome (2028 delinking, FTC 10-year monitoring, state PBM laws), and Q3 showed the PBM repricing is real: Pharmacy Benefit Services income -25% YTD. Base 50% as the company's own conversion plan plus guidance. Bull stays at 20%: the Investor Day put a number on it (10-14% EPS CAGR) but a target is not evidence, and it still needs cost-plus to win share AND margins to hold through 2028 AND specialty mix to expand. Would move bear down toward 25% on a 2027 outlook showing PBS income stabilising; up if HCSC or a Centene-scale contract re-bids away.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
